Do not use it for S3, EFS, FSx,\\\\n  instance store, or EC2 problems unrelated to EBS.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: dewavic\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, INCIDENT_RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EBS, Amazon EC2, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS KMS, AWS CloudTrail, Service Quotas\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Storage\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n# Amazon EBS Expertise\\\\n\\\\nUse this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account\\'s Amazon EBS setup. Approval is given only on the approval card. A typed \\\\\"approve\\\\\" in chat is not approval.\\\\n- **Discover, don\\'t assume:** read every configuration value from the APIs.\\\\n- **Rule EBS in or out before tuning it.**\\\\n- **Answer the asked question first;** other findings go under \\\\\"Separate findings\\\\\".\\\\n- **Always check the instance layer** and size changes within the instance\\'s EBS **baseline**.\\\\n- **Never recommend more provisioning for an impairment.**\\\\n- **Use current service rules:** up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours. {"id": "5c0d6c4f-16cb-4fc3-b273-22c2dfacfc9d", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_LC5mzc6Qp304t21vT8plGU", "content": "[{'text': '# Review mode: Amazon EBS operational review\\n\\nReview mode answers \"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\". It is entirely read-only. Run each area per Region, rate each finding with the scale in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md), and write the report with [review-report-format.md](review-report-format.md).\\n\\nThe Capacity and quota headroom section is also a shared capability. Troubleshoot paths use it when an operation failed on a limit.\\n\\n## Capacity and quota headroom\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\nRun every check below even when the error looks simple. A user who reports a quota error has already failed to fix it alone, so give documented findings in the verdict format, not a short chat reply. Whether the run is a chat or a formal investigation is decided by how the user starts it, not by this skill.\\n\\n1. If an operation failed, quote the error and name the quota it refers to. For example \"You have exceeded your maximum io2 IOPS limit of 100000 IOPS in this region\" refers to the regional io2 IOPS quota, which is separate from the per-volume maximum.\\n2. `ListServiceQuotas --service-code ebs`: quota name, code, applied `Value`, `Adjustable`. Find quotas by name; never hardcode codes. `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota` shows the default.\\n3. Compute usage from the inventory:\\n   - Provisioned IOPS: sum of `Iops` for io1 volumes and for io2 volumes, separately.\\n   - Storage per type: sum of `Size` per volume type, converted from GiB to TiB.\\n   - Snapshots per Region: count of `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self`.\\n   - Fast snapshot restore: `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores` count of enabled entries.\\n4. `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` for pending requests. Never propose a duplicate.\\n\\n**Rating rule**\\n\\n- Usage at or above 80% of the applied quota is flagged. The 80% value is configurable; ask the operator if they use a different one.\\n- A quota that blocked an operation is `High`.\\n- A quota flagged at or above the threshold is `Medium`, or `High` if the user states a planned increase that would exceed it.\\n- Unreadable quota or usage is `Indeterminate`.\\n\\n**Fix**\\n\\n- Adjustable: a pre-filled Service Quotas request (service code `ebs`, quota code as read, desired value) proposed as a directed action. The desired value is the user\\'s stated need, or current usage plus the request that failed. No fixed multipliers.\\n- Not adjustable: draft the AWS Support case text (service, quota name, Region, desired value, business justification).\\n- Name the quotas that commonly cause problems: per-Region IOPS for io1 and io2, per-Region storage per volume type, snapshots per Region, and fast snapshot restore.\\n\\n## Observability\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EBS namespace: alarms on `VolumeQueueLength`, latency (`VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency`, or `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeTotalWriteTime` math), throughput, and `BurstBalance` for gp2, st1 and sc1.\\n2. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EC2 namespace: `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` on instances that publish them.\\n3. Which volumes are critical: ask the operator, or use tags they name. Do not infer criticality from tag values by yourself.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical volume with no Amazon EBS alarm is `Medium`. `High` if the operator says the volume backs a production database or service. An alarm in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` for a long time is `Low` (it may be on a deleted volume).\\n\\n**Fix**: propose alarms with metric, dimensions (`VolumeAvg*` need `VolumeId` and `InstanceId`) and the threshold the operator chooses.\\n\\n## Cost hygiene\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. gp2 volumes: gp3 candidates. gp3 has 20% lower price per GiB than gp2 and includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s.\\n2. Unattached volumes: `DescribeVolumes` with `status=available`.\\n3. Over-provisioned IOPS or throughput: measured vs provisioned, and provisioned above the instance EBS baseline (see [troubleshoot-billing.md](troubleshoot-billing.md) step 6).\\n4. AWS Compute Optimizer `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` if enabled (optional).\\n\\n**Rating rule**: `Low` by default. `Medium` when the operator names cost as a goal or the resource is large relative to the account\\'s Amazon EBS spend as shown in Cost Explorer.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyVolume` to gp3 with IOPS and throughput sized as in [troubleshoot-volume-modification.md](troubleshoot-volume-modification.md) step 6; snapshot then delete for unattached volumes. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Resilience\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. Inventory volumes (`DescribeVolumes`), including root volumes.\\n2. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: `GetLifecyclePolicies` (state `ENABLED`) and `GetLifecyclePolicy` for target tags and resource type. Target tags are case sensitive. Note default policies, which target the Region\\'s volumes or instances without recent backups.\\n3. AWS Backup: `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection` (selection by resource ARN, by tag condition, or all resources of a type), and `ListProtectedResources`.\\n4. Match each volume to a policy or a selection. A volume that matches none is unprotected.\\n5. For protected volumes, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true for the latest recovery point, and the latest `aws:dlm:*` tagged snapshot of the volume. Compare its age with the policy schedule. Without that parameter, the call also returns manual snapshots, which are not backups from the plan.\\n6. Cross-Region copy for disaster recovery: copy actions in DLM policies or AWS Backup copy rules.\\n7. Ask the operator for their recovery point objective. Do not assume one.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: an unprotected volume the operator calls critical is `High`. A protected volume whose latest recovery point is older than its own schedule is `High` (the backup may be failing). No cross-Region copy where the operator needs Regional disaster recovery is `Medium`. Unprotected non-critical volumes are `Low`.\\n\\n**Fix**: tag the volume to match an existing policy, add it to a backup selection, or create a policy. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Encryption posture\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault` and `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId` per Region.\\n2. Unencrypted volumes and snapshots (`Encrypted` is false).\\n3. For keys in use, AWS KMS `DescribeKey` state. A disabled or pending-deletion key in use is a risk.\\n4. Snapshot exposure: `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState` per Region, and `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self --restorable-by-user-ids all` for snapshots that are public now.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a key in use that is disabled or pending deletion is `High`. A public snapshot is `High`. Encryption by default off is `Medium`. Unencrypted volumes are `Medium`, or `High` if the operator says the data is regulated. Snapshot block public access in the `unblocked` state is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: turn on encryption by default; re-encrypt with the steps in [troubleshoot-encryption.md](troubleshoot-encryption.md); turn on snapshot block public access (`block-all-sharing`, or `block-new-sharing` while existing public shares are reviewed). All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Deletion protection\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeInstanceAttribute --attribute blockDeviceMapping` for `DeleteOnTermination` on each attached volume. A data volume with `DeleteOnTermination` true is deleted when the instance terminates.\\n2. Recycle Bin `ListRules` for `EBS_SNAPSHOT` (and for AMIs if the account uses them).\\n3. Snapshot lock: `DescribeLockedSnapshots` for snapshots the operator must keep.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical data volume with `DeleteOnTermination` true is `High`. No Recycle Bin rule for snapshots is `Medium`. No lock on snapshots the operator says are compliance records is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyInstanceAttribute` to set `DeleteOnTermination` false on the data volume, a Recycle Bin retention rule, or a snapshot lock. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- Review mode is entirely read-only. It never runs a mutating call.\\n- Every fix is listed under \"Proposed actions\" in the report with exact parameters, expected effect, cost direction and rollback. Each one needs a directed action approved on the approval card.\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon EBS quotas: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/ebs-service.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-resource-quotas.html\\n- Requesting a quota increase: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/latest/userguide/request-quota-increase.html\\n- Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon EBS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/using_cloudwatch_ebs.html\\n- gp3 and gp2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html\\n- Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-lifecycle.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-ami-policy.html\\n- AWS Backup resource assignment: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/assigning-resources.html\\n- Encryption by default: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/encryption-by-default.html\\n- Block public access for snapshots: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/block-public-access-snapshots.html\\n- AWS Backup ListRecoveryPointsByResource: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/APIReference/API_ListRecoveryPointsByResource.html\\n- DeleteOnTermination: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/terminating-instances.html\\n- Recycle Bin: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/recycle-bin.html\\n- Snapshot lock: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshot-lock.html\\n- Fast snapshot restore: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-fast-snapshot-restore.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_jPAEsWTnTvrlWc5Pr1lEzd", "content": "[{'text': '# Data collection: read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks\\n\\nLoad this file on every request. Every value in a verdict or a review comes from one of these calls. For example \"Not stuck. The modification is in `optimizing`, which already applies the new IOPS.\"\\n2. **Evidence.** The values that support the answer, each with units and the time window (for example \"average `<value>` IOPS, `<start>` to `<end>` UTC\"). Throughput in MiB/s.\\n3. **Binding layer.** One of: Volume, Instance, Burst credits, Quota, Not EBS, AWS-side impairment, Not applicable.\\n4. **Recommendation.** Exact parameters (volume ID, dimension, target value, how the target was computed), or \"No change\". Is the summed IOPS or MiB/s of all attached volumes flat at the instance EBS baseline, or are `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%` draining or at 0?\\n   - Yes: **Instance**. Is the instance healthy and one volume flat at its own provisioned limit on the dimension its type is judged by?\\n   - Yes: **Volume**.\\n3. Are all layers below their limits, latency at the volume\\'s normal level, and queue length low?\\n   - Yes: **Not EBS**. Check CPU, memory, network and the application.\\n6. Are all layers below their limits but latency and `VolumeQueueLength` up while IOPS and throughput collapse?\\n   - Yes: **AWS-side impairment** (or injected latency). Go to the decision tree |\\n| Low | Normal | Low | Neither. Check network, locks and the application |\\n\\n\"High\" and \"normal\" mean compared with the same resource\\'s own history and the type\\'s documented expectation in [metrics-thresholds.md](metrics-thresholds.md).\\n\\n## Escalation (shared capability)\\n\\nEscalate to AWS Support when either is true:\\n\\n- Scope signals: an open AWS Health event for the volume, Availability Zone or Region; several resources failing the same way; `DescribeVolumeStatus` reports the volume as impaired or a failing status check.\\n- A bounded investigation cannot explain the symptom: all layers below limits, no running AWS FIS experiment, no recent change, and the symptom persists.\\n\\nSpecific cases:\\n\\n- Attach or detach stuck: the attachment stays in `attaching` or `detaching` and does not progress. {"id": "064540c2-a169-4dbb-bcb7-c17465e71143", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "# EBS pre-launch review: account 012345678901_1, us-east-1

**Not production-ready yet.** I found no High-severity issues, but several Medium findings should be fixed or consciously accepted before launch. The biggest are instance limits that throttle your volumes, almost no backups, and no encryption.

I haven't confirmed which volumes are production-critical or what your recovery point objective (RPO) is, and I didn't infer either from tags. Several ratings below would rise to High once you tell me.

The review was read-only and covered 24 volumes (9 root, 9 attached data, 6 unattached), 9 snapshots, 10 instances, and 35 EBS quotas.

## Summary

| Area | Rating | Main reason |
|---|---|---|
| Capacity and quota headroom | OK | Every quota is under 25% used, and no quota requests are pending. |
| Observability | Medium | There are almost no latency, burst-balance, or instance-balance alarms. |
| Cost hygiene | Medium | Volumes are provisioned beyond what their instances can deliver. |
| Resilience | Low, provisional | 23 of 24 volumes have no backup. This becomes High for any volume you call critical. |
| Encryption posture | Medium | Encryption by default is off, and all volumes and snapshots are unencrypted. |
| Deletion protection | Indeterminate | I couldn't read Recycle Bin rules. |

## Fix before launch

**1. Volumes provisioned above what their instance can deliver.** This is the most important finding.
- **i-0123456789abcdef0_2 (t3.medium):** the attached io2 volume vol-0123456789abcdef0_5 is provisioned at 20,000 IOPS. The instance maximum is 11,800 IOPS, and the volume has only used about 0.35 IOPS at peak over 14 days.
- **i-0123456789abcdef0_4 (t3.micro):** its volumes total 19,000 IOPS against the same 11,800 maximum, and 250 MiB/s of gp3 throughput against a 10.37 MiB/s baseline.
  - `EBSIOBalance%` hit 0% in the last ~3.5 hours, so it is already exhausting burst credits.
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_24 (16,000 IOPS) peaked at 11,807 IOPS, which is the instance ceiling.
- **i-0123456789abcdef0_3 (c6i.xlarge) and i-0123456789abcdef0_6 (t3.micro):** provisioned above the instance baseline but under the maximum.

Raising volume IOPS won't help here. Either right-size the volumes or move to a larger, non-burstable instance. If these instances will carry launch traffic, a t3.micro is a risk.

**2. Volumes already at their own limits.** vol-0123456789abcdef0_18 (io2) peaked at exactly its 1,000 provisioned IOPS, and vol-0123456789abcdef0 (gp3) peaked at exactly its 125 MiB/s. Both show queueing, with queue lengths of about 1.4 and 10.3. Both were created today, so there's only ~3.5 hours of data, and 5-minute averages can hide shorter bursts. Re-test them under realistic load.

**3. Backups.** Only vol-0123456789abcdef0_3 has backup coverage. Its DLM policy `hourly-keep-2` took its latest snapshot about 25 minutes before the review. That volume is also unattached.
- The other 23 volumes have no AWS Backup protection and no DLM snapshot.
- The AWS Backup plan "Trial" has no resource selection, so it protects nothing.
- I couldn't read DLM policies (the call was blocked), so coverage by other policies, cross-Region copies, and the "keep-2" versus 3 snapshots discrepancy are all unconfirmed.

**4. Encryption.**
- Encryption by default is off in us-east-1. This is easy to fix and affects new volumes only.
- All 24 volumes and all 9 snapshots are unencrypted, which is Medium, or High if the data is regulated.
- Snapshot block public access is `unblocked`. No public snapshots exist today, so enabling `block-all-sharing` is low-risk.
- I found no disabled or pending-deletion KMS keys. No customer-managed key is in use.

**5. Alarms.**
- Only 3 volumes have queue-length alarms, and none have latency alarms.
- None of the 7 gp2 or st1 volumes has a `BurstBalance` alarm.
- Only one instance has an `EBSIOBalance%` alarm, and there are no `EBSByteBalance%` alarms. i-0123456789abcdef0_9, i-0123456789abcdef0_3, and i-0123456789abcdef0_4 publish these metrics but have no alarms on them.
- The alarm on i-0123456789abcdef0_12 has been in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` since April 2025, and that instance doesn't exist. It's stale.

## Lower priority

- **gp2 to gp3:** 7 gp2 volumes (64 GiB total) are gp3 candidates. gp3 is 20% cheaper per GiB and includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s.
- **Unattached volumes:** 6 are in `available` state, totaling 287 GiB.
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_4 has been idle since 2023-11-13.
  - vol-0123456789abcdef0_8 and vol-0123456789abcdef0_12 carry 6,000 IOPS and 250 MiB/s while idle.
- **Over-provisioning:** vol-0123456789abcdef0_7 peaked at about 500 IOPS and 125 MiB/s against 6,000 IOPS and 250 MiB/s provisioned. There's too little history to judge.
- **Deletion protection:** all 9 data volumes have `DeleteOnTermination=false`, which is good. Root volumes use the default `true`. No snapshot locks exist.

## What I couldn't check

- **Recycle Bin rules and DLM policies:** both calls were blocked in this agent space, so snapshot recovery after deletion is unconfirmed.
- **t2.micro instances** (i-0123456789abcdef0_11, i-0123456789abcdef0_10, i-0123456789abcdef0_5): no EBS baseline data was available.
- **7 volumes on stopped instances** have no metrics. Most other volumes were created today and have only ~3.5 hours of history, so the peaks aren't representative of launch load.
- **Not reviewed:** alarm actions (SNS targets), Compute Optimizer, Cost Explorer spend share, and other Regions.

## Proposed changes

I haven't run any of these. Each needs your approval.
1. Right-size volume IOPS or instance type on i-0123456789abcdef0_2 and i-0123456789abcdef0_4.
2. Create the `BurstBalance`, queue-length, latency, `EBSIOBalance%`, and `EBSByteBalance%` alarms. You choose the thresholds.
3. Enable EBS encryption by default and snapshot block public access.
4. Put the volumes you confirm as needing protection into an AWS Backup selection or DLM policy.
5. Re-encrypt critical volumes and snapshots. This needs downtime for in-use volumes.
6. Convert gp2 volumes to gp3, and snapshot then clean up idle unattached volumes.
7. Delete or re-point the stale alarm.

Tell me which volumes are production-critical, whether any data is regulated, and your RPO. I can then re-rate the findings and give exact parameters for the changes you want. Several volumes carry `Project=ebs-skill-eval` tags, so some of this may be test infrastructure, but I haven't treated that as confirmation.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

It is entirely read-only. Run each area per Region, rate each finding with the scale in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md), and write the report with [review-report-format.md](review-report-format.md).\\n\\nThe Capacity and quota headroom section is also a shared capability. Troubleshoot paths use it when an operation failed on a limit.\\n\\n## Capacity and quota headroom\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\nRun every check below even when the error looks simple. A user who reports a quota error has already failed to fix it alone, so give documented findings in the verdict format, not a short chat reply. Whether the run is a chat or a formal investigation is decided by how the user starts it, not by this skill.\\n\\n1. If an operation failed, quote the error and name the quota it refers to. For example \"You have exceeded your maximum io2 IOPS limit of 100000 IOPS in this region\" refers to the regional io2 IOPS quota, which is separate from the per-volume maximum.\\n2. `ListServiceQuotas --service-code ebs`: quota name, code, applied `Value`, `Adjustable`. Find quotas by name; never hardcode codes. `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota` shows the default.\\n3. Compute usage from the inventory:\\n   - Provisioned IOPS: sum of `Iops` for io1 volumes and for io2 volumes, separately.\\n   - Storage per type: sum of `Size` per volume type, converted from GiB to TiB.\\n   - Snapshots per Region: count of `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self`.\\n   - Fast snapshot restore: `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores` count of enabled entries.\\n4. `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` for pending requests. Never propose a duplicate.\\n\\n**Rating rule**\\n\\n- Usage at or above 80% of the applied quota is flagged. The 80% value is configurable; ask the operator if they use a different one.\\n- A quota that blocked an operation is `High`.\\n- A quota flagged at or above the threshold is `Medium`, or `High` if the user states a planned increase that would exceed it.\\n- Unreadable quota or usage is `Indeterminate`.\\n\\n**Fix**\\n\\n- Adjustable: a pre-filled Service Quotas request (service code `ebs`, quota code as read, desired value) proposed as a directed action. The desired value is the user\\'s stated need, or current usage plus the request that failed. No fixed multipliers.\\n- Not adjustable: draft the AWS Support case text (service, quota name, Region, desired value, business justification).\\n- Name the quotas that commonly cause problems: per-Region IOPS for io1 and io2, per-Region storage per volume type, snapshots per Region, and fast snapshot restore.\\n\\n## Observability\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EBS namespace: alarms on `VolumeQueueLength`, latency (`VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency`, or `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeTotalWriteTime` math), throughput, and `BurstBalance` for gp2, st1 and sc1.\\n2. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EC2 namespace: `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` on instances that publish them.\\n3. Which volumes are critical: ask the operator, or use tags they name. Unattached volumes: `DescribeVolumes` with `status=available`.\\n3. Over-provisioned IOPS or throughput: measured vs provisioned, and provisioned above the instance EBS baseline (see [troubleshoot-billing.md](troubleshoot-billing.md) step 6).\\n4. AWS Compute Optimizer `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` if enabled (optional).\\n\\n**Rating rule**: `Low` by default. `Medium` when the operator names cost as a goal or the resource is large relative to the account\\'s Amazon EBS spend as shown in Cost Explorer.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyVolume` to gp3 with IOPS and throughput sized as in [troubleshoot-volume-modification.md](troubleshoot-volume-modification.md) step 6; snapshot then delete for unattached volumes. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: `GetLifecyclePolicies` (state `ENABLED`) and `GetLifecyclePolicy` for target tags and resource type. Target tags are case sensitive. Note default policies, which target the Region\\'s volumes or instances without recent backups.\\n3. AWS Backup: `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection` (selection by resource ARN, by tag condition, or all resources of a type), and `ListProtectedResources`.\\n4. For protected volumes, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true for the latest recovery point, and the latest `aws:dlm:*` tagged snapshot of the volume. Do not assume one.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: an unprotected volume the operator calls critical is `High`. A protected volume whose latest recovery point is older than its own schedule is `High` (the backup may be failing). No cross-Region copy where the operator needs Regional disaster recovery is `Medium`. Unprotected non-critical volumes are `Low`.\\n\\n**Fix**: tag the volume to match an existing policy, add it to a backup selection, or create a policy. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Encryption posture\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault` and `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId` per Region.\\n2. Unencrypted volumes and snapshots (`Encrypted` is false).\\n3. For keys in use, AWS KMS `DescribeKey` state. A disabled or pending-deletion key in use is a risk.\\n4. Snapshot exposure: `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState` per Region, and `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self --restorable-by-user-ids all` for snapshots that are public now.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a key in use that is disabled or pending deletion is `High`. Snapshot block public access in the `unblocked` state is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: turn on encryption by default; re-encrypt with the steps in [troubleshoot-encryption.md](troubleshoot-encryption.md); turn on snapshot block public access (`block-all-sharing`, or `block-new-sharing` while existing public shares are reviewed). All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Deletion protection\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeInstanceAttribute --attribute blockDeviceMapping` for `DeleteOnTermination` on each attached volume. No Recycle Bin rule for snapshots is `Medium`. No lock on snapshots the operator says are compliance records is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyInstanceAttribute` to set `DeleteOnTermination` false on the data volume, a Recycle Bin retention rule, or a snapshot lock. It never runs a mutating call.\\n- Every fix is listed under \"Proposed actions\" in the report with exact parameters, expected effect, cost direction and rollback. Use `Sum` statistics for ops, bytes and time.\\n\\n- IOPS = Sum(`VolumeReadOps` + `VolumeWriteOps`) / period in seconds\\n- MiB/s = Sum(`VolumeReadBytes` + `VolumeWriteBytes`) / period in seconds / 1,048,576\\n- Average latency per operation = `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeReadOps` (and the write equivalent)\\n- Idle percentage = Sum(`VolumeIdleTime`) / period in seconds x 100\\n- MiB/s from `VolumeAvgThroughput` = value in KiB/s / 1,024\\n\\nWhat a 1-minute average hides: sub-minute peaks can reach a limit while the minute average looks below it (micro-bursting). For example \"Not stuck. The modification is in `optimizing`, which already applies the new IOPS.\"\\n2. **Evidence.** The values that support the answer, each with units and the time window (for example \"average `<value>` IOPS, `<start>` to `<end>` UTC\"). Mutating steps are proposals for a directed action.\\n5. **Separate findings.** Other true facts, labelled so they never change the Answer. For example a modification that succeeded on a volume whose instance caps delivered IOPS: the cap goes here, never as \"the modification failed\".\\n6. **Gaps.** What could not be checked and why (API denied, approval gate, metric absent).\\n\\n## Binding-layer decision tree\\n\\nWork through it in order. Use measured values and the limits read from the APIs. Do not use fixed percentage triggers.\\n\\n1. Is the summed IOPS or MiB/s of all attached volumes flat at the instance EBS baseline, or are `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%` draining or at 0?\\n   - Yes: **Instance**. Say \"the volume has headroom; raising volume IOPS will not help; change the instance type\". ## 4. Deletion protection

All nine non-root (data) volumes have `DeleteOnTermination = false`. Root volumes have `true`, which is the default. I read these from `DescribeInstances` block device mappings.

## Not checked / Gaps

- **`rbin:ListRules` (EBS_SNAPSHOT).** The call was blocked as gated in this agent space. Recycle Bin protection is unconfirmed. I did not try `GetRule` or any workaround.
- **`DescribeInstanceAttribute`.** I did not call it. I used `DescribeInstances` block device mappings for `DeleteOnTermination` instead.
- **`ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota`.** I used the service-wide `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistory` for `ebs` instead, which returned empty.

- **t2.micro instances** i-0123456789abcdef0_11, i-0123456789abcdef0_10 and i-0123456789abcdef0_5, plus the stopped-instance volumes. There is no baseline or metric data, so they were not assessed.
- **Short metric history.** Most volumes have only about 3.5 hours of data, and 7 volumes have none, so peak statistics are not representative of launch load.
- **Alarm checks.** I did not check alarm actions (SNS targets) or alarm period and evaluation settings.
- **Out of scope.** Resilience and encryption belong to the other agent. The Trusted Advisor and DynamoDB alarms, including some in `ALARM`, are not EBS.
- **Other Regions.** Not covered.

## Proposed actions (none executed; each needs operator-approved directed action)

1. Create alarms: `BurstBalance` on the seven gp2/st1 volumes, `VolumeQueueLength` and latency on volumes the operator names, and `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` on i-0123456789abcdef0_2, i-0123456789abcdef0_9, i-0123456789abcdef0_3 and i-0123456789abcdef0_4. The operator chooses thresholds.
2. Right-size the instance/volume mismatch before launch: i-0123456789abcdef0_2 (io2 20,000 IOPS against an 11,800 maximum) and i-0123456789abcdef0_4 (16,000 + 3,000 IOPS against 11,800, with `EBSIOBalance%` at 0%).
3. `ModifyVolume` the gp2 volumes to gp3 (cost down, rollback by modifying back).
4. Snapshot then delete idle `available` volumes, and trim their IOPS and throughput.
5. Remove or re-point the stale alarm on i-0123456789abcdef0_12.
6. Have the operator confirm Recycle Bin rules, and decide on snapshot locks.

**Next steps.** The operator should confirm which volumes are production-critical, because that would raise several Medium findings to High. They should also re-run the peak-load check once the stopped instances have run under realistic load.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
